common.tagline: Research on sound visualization and media art
footer.statement: From the physical structure of sound to animal ultrasound, human perception, and the artistic treatment of environmental recordings. Research notes on what lies beyond hearing.
footer.dataNote: Research results and measurement data are published only when sources and conditions can be documented.
home.hero.lead: The physical structure of sound, ultrasonic animal vocalization, the correspondence between hearing and color, and the artistic treatment of environmental recordings. This project crosses those layers of listening through measurement and visualization.
home.ticker: FFT spectral analysis / spectral centroid / ultrasonic vocalization / cross-modal correspondence / field recording / generative art
home.areas.title: Research areas
home.areas.lead: Four projects approach sound from different distances. What is measured, how it is transformed, and how it is presented differ, but the underlying question is shared: how can the boundaries of hearing be made visible?
home.areas.visualization.title: Sound Visualization
home.areas.visualization.desc: A visualization tool that turns acoustic features into color and form, built around an existing p5.js sketch.
home.areas.rat.title: Rat Vocalization
home.areas.rat.desc: Recording and analyzing rat ultrasonic vocalizations to visualize acoustic structure beyond the human hearing range.
home.areas.perception.title: Sound & Perception
home.areas.perception.desc: An experimental inquiry into how pitch and roughness relate to hue, lightness, and saturation.
home.areas.atlas.title: Sound Atlas
home.areas.atlas.desc: A concept for selecting recording locations on a globe and experiencing environmental sound alongside generative art.
home.method.title: Measure, transform, experience
home.method.lead: The analysis algorithm stays as it is. What gets designed is how its output is mapped into color and form.
home.method.step1.title: Record
home.method.step1.desc: Microphones, recorders, and open datasets. Acquisition conditions and rights are documented.
home.method.step2.title: Analyze
home.method.step2.desc: Frequency analysis by FFT and feature extraction, using the existing implementation unchanged.
home.method.step3.title: Transform
home.method.step3.desc: Amplitude, spectral centroid, and flatness are mapped to lightness, hue, and saturation.
home.method.step4.title: Present
home.method.step4.desc: Presented as a p5.js sketch, a printed figure, or an interactive screen.
home.method.note: The analysis and presentation layers are separated, so the expression can change without touching the algorithm.
home.current.title: Current work
home.current.ratQuestion: How does the temporal structure of ultrasonic vocalization change with context?
home.current.ratBody: The recording, preprocessing, and feature-extraction workflow is being assembled. No measurements or analysis results are published yet; conditions will be published alongside them once confirmed.
home.current.dataBody: Research results and experimental data are published only when reproducible conditions and sources have been verified. Numbers are never published ahead of that check.
home.current.statusItem1: Visualization: page structure published, sketch awaiting integration
home.current.statusItem2: Rat study: method being organized, data unpublished
home.publications.title: Publications
home.publications.lead: Graduation research, conference presentations, writing, and exhibitions. Confirmed entries are being compiled.
home.publications.empty: No entries have been registered yet
home.closing.title: Look beyond the audible.
home.closing.body: The background of the research and the technical structure behind the visualization.
visualization.title: Sound Visualization
visualization.jpTitle: Turning acoustic features into color and form
visualization.lead: Sound from a microphone or an audio file is analyzed with FFT, and features such as amplitude, spectral centroid, and flatness are translated into hue, lightness, saturation, and contour movement. An existing p5.js sketch sits at the core and will be integrated into the page in stages.
visualization.stage.label: LIVE STAGE
visualization.stage.caption: This area receives analyzed acoustic features and draws color and form. The existing sketch is not modified; it will be mounted onto this stage.
visualization.stage.placeholder: The figure is a layout placeholder. It does not represent audio data.
visualization.mapping.title: Draft mapping
visualization.mapping.lead: Using the existing analysis output as input, this is an attempt to decide which feature drives which visual channel. The mapping below is a pre-validation proposal, not a confirmed correspondence.
visualization.mapping.row1.intent: Let intensity read as the brightness of a surface
visualization.mapping.row2.intent: Shift higher sounds toward cooler hues
visualization.mapping.row3.intent: Increase color intensity as the signal becomes noisier
visualization.mapping.row4.intent: Express low resonance as instability of outline
visualization.reuse.title: An architecture that leaves analysis untouched
visualization.reuse.lead: The research algorithm is left alone. Only the input and output boundary is defined.
visualization.reuse.layer1.title: Analysis layer
visualization.reuse.layer1.desc: The existing FFT analysis and color conversion. Neither parameters nor calculation order change.
visualization.reuse.layer2.title: Transform layer
visualization.reuse.layer2.desc: An adapter that shapes analysis output into the feature set the display needs.
visualization.reuse.layer3.title: Presentation layer
visualization.reuse.layer3.desc: Drawing by the p5.js sketch, isolated so it can be replaced.
visualization.reuse.note: Integration loads the existing setup / draw unchanged and connects only the feature hand-off.
visualization.next.title: Next steps
visualization.next.item1: Export the existing p5.js sketch and mount it on the stage
visualization.next.item2: Switch between microphone and audio-file input
visualization.next.item3: Tune mapping parameters and export still frames for documentation
rat.title: Rat Vocalization
rat.jpTitle: Analyzing and visualizing rat ultrasonic vocalization
rat.lead: Rats vocalize in an ultrasonic range that humans cannot hear. This study records the temporal structure and frequency content of those calls, and turns sound beyond the audible range into something that can be observed.
rat.question.title: Research questions
rat.question.q1: How does the temporal structure of vocalization change with social context or environment?
rat.question.q2: What becomes visible when ultrasonic content is shown alongside the human hearing range?
rat.question.q3: How far can an inaudible sound be validly translated into perceivable color and form?
rat.background.title: Background
rat.background.p1: It is widely reported that rat vocalizations extend above the human hearing range. The literature describes distinct call types in a lower and a higher ultrasonic band, used according to context.
rat.background.p2: Starting from that general background, this project aims to make the structure of recorded sound observable first-hand. The figure below is a conceptual schematic, not a measurement from this project.
rat.figure.title: Frequency band schematic
rat.figure.caption: Schematic: a conceptual arrangement based on general literature. Not a measurement or analysis result from this project.
rat.method.title: Method (planned)
rat.method.step1.title: Recording
rat.method.step1.desc: Recorded with ultrasound-capable microphones and a documented sampling chain.
rat.method.step2.title: Preprocessing
rat.method.step2.desc: Noise reduction and segment extraction, with processing conditions kept reproducible.
rat.method.step3.title: Features
rat.method.step3.desc: Frequency content, duration, and inter-call interval are extracted with the existing analysis code.
rat.method.step4.title: Visualization
rat.method.step4.desc: Presented both as a spectrogram and as a color mapping, so interpretations can be compared.
rat.data.title: Data availability
rat.data.body: Measurement data and analysis results are not currently published. When released, recording conditions, preprocessing, and analysis settings will be included.
rat.ethics.title: Recording and ethics
rat.ethics.body: Any recording involving animals follows the guidelines and approvals of the affiliated institution. A summary of the recording environment and procedure will be included at publication.
perception.title: Sound & Perception
perception.jpTitle: Thinking about sound and color through experiment
perception.lead: Do qualities of hearing such as pitch, loudness, and roughness correspond to hue, lightness, and saturation in ways shared across individuals? Rather than borrowing popular claims from color psychology, the project tests this through rating experiments.
perception.question.title: Research questions
perception.question.q1: How much is the correspondence between pitch and hue shaped by learning and culture?
perception.question.q2: Does roughness of sound consistently relate to impressions of saturation?
perception.question.q3: Does the correspondence differ when a sound is heard rather than seen as a visual trace?
perception.axes.title: Correspondences under consideration
perception.axes.lead: These are hypotheses organized for study. They precede experimental validation and are not established findings.
perception.design.title: Experiment design (draft)
perception.design.step1.title: Stimulus design
perception.design.step1.desc: Short stimuli with controlled acoustic features, paired with a corresponding color palette.
perception.design.step2.title: Rating
perception.design.step2.desc: Participants rate the fit between sound and color; response time is also recorded.
perception.design.step3.title: Analysis
perception.design.step3.desc: Individual difference and shared structure are analyzed separately, feeding back into the color mapping design.
perception.data.title: Public data
perception.data.body: The experiment is at the design stage; no participant data or results are published. Stimuli, procedure, and analysis conditions will be documented at release.
perception.caution.title: A note on citation
perception.caution.body: Popular claims about color psychology include statements that have not been thoroughly tested. This project keeps documented findings separate from its own experimental results.
atlas.title: Sound Atlas
atlas.jpTitle: Experiencing sound and generative art through place
atlas.lead: A page for selecting recording locations around the world on a globe, then experiencing the environmental sound of that place together with forms generated from the sound. Location data and audio will be registered from here on.
atlas.globe.label: 3D GLOBE
atlas.globe.caption: Because no location data is registered yet, a conceptual figure is shown. Once implemented, this area will hold a rotating globe with selectable locations.
atlas.empty.title: No recording locations have been registered yet
atlas.empty.body: Once publishable audio and location information are available, the location list and audio player will appear here.
atlas.empty.note: No placeholder locations, audio, or generated artwork have been added.
atlas.flow.title: How it will work
atlas.flow.step1.title: Choose a location
atlas.flow.step1.desc: Select a recording location from a marker on the globe or from the list.
atlas.flow.step2.title: Listen to the place
atlas.flow.step2.desc: Play the recording made there and review when and how it was captured.
atlas.flow.step3.title: See the generated art
atlas.flow.step3.desc: Forms generated from the acoustic features are displayed in sync with the sound.
atlas.tech.title: Technical plan
atlas.tech.audioValue: Publishable recordings only, with sources noted.
atlas.tech.artValue: Forms generated from acoustic features. p5.js intended.
atlas.rights.title: How recordings are handled
atlas.rights.body: Recordings made by third parties are published only after confirming permission and source. Location information is shown only at the precision consented to.

about.title: About
about.lead: Sound is not received by the ear alone. It resonates in the body, suggests color and form, and attaches itself to the memory of a place. This project approaches those connections from the side of measurement and visualization.
about.background.title: Background
about.background.p1: Acoustic analysis is used not only in music production and environmental assessment, but also in animal behavior research and media art. Yet the design decision of how to present an analysis is often buried inside an individual implementation.
about.background.p2: This research keeps the analysis algorithm as a shared foundation while describing, in a verifiable way, the process of translating its output into color, form, and motion. Working with sound beyond the audible range is an extension of that aim.
about.approach.title: Approach
about.approach.a1.title: Measure
about.approach.a1.desc: Amplitude, spectral centroid, and flatness are extracted on top of FFT-based frequency analysis.
about.approach.a2.title: Transform
about.approach.a2.desc: Acoustic features are mapped to visual channels, with the basis for each mapping written down.
about.approach.a3.title: Make it experienceable
about.approach.a3.desc: Presented as sketches, figures, or a globe that a viewer can operate.
about.stack.title: Technology
about.stack.p5: p5.js — the existing FFT and color-conversion sketch is the core.
about.stack.web: Web Audio API — input capture and preprocessing.
about.stack.react: React / TypeScript — page structure and state.
about.stack.note: The analysis algorithm is not modified; a transform layer sits between analysis and presentation.
about.profile.title: Profile
about.profile.body: Name, affiliation, and contact details are being prepared for publication. A research contact address will be added here once confirmed.
about.roadmap.title: Release plan
about.roadmap.p1: 1. Site structure and the basic frame of each page (current)
about.roadmap.p2: 2. Integration of the existing p5.js sketch and release of the visualization page
about.roadmap.p3: 3. Organization and release of research data, then the globe implementation
